name: African Grandmothers' Remedies
summary: Tangawizi, rooibos, bissap, baobab and soft uji from across Africa.

remedies.name: Tangawizi Tea
remedies.howItHelps: East African ginger tea warms the throat and helps a stuffy nose.
steps: Grown-up boils grated ginger in water.
Add a squeeze of lemon and a little honey.
remedies.caution: Honey is fine for big kids, never for babies under one year.

remedies.name: Rooibos Tea
remedies.howItHelps: South African red bush tea has no caffeine. Grandmothers give it warm for sore tummies; scientists are still studying it.

remedies.name: Bissap / Zobo
remedies.howItHelps: A cool hibiscus drink from West Africa that helps you drink more on hot days. Go easy on sugar!
steps: Steep dried hibiscus petals in water.
Strain, add a little ginger and chill.

remedies.name: Baobab Drink
remedies.howItHelps: Baobab fruit powder has vitamin C and fiber. A cooling drink in Senegal.
steps: Stir baobab powder into cool water.

remedies.name: Thin Uji
remedies.howItHelps: Thin, warm porridge is the gentle food grandmothers give a sick child.
steps: Cook millet or maize flour in lots of water.

remedies.name: Aloe Leaf Gel
remedies.howItHelps: Cool aloe gel calms itchy, swollen skin.
steps: Dab the clear gel on the bite.
